Rung in affectionate memory of Philip “Phil” C. Pitchford whose funeral took place earlier today.

Phil or “Uncle Phil” as he was affectionately known by some members of this band, was a former member of the local band at Brant Broughton for many years and rang in the first peal (Grandsire Doubles) on the bells by an all Sunday Service band in 1959.
Phil rang 16 peals of Grandsire Doubles, all of them rung at Brant Broughton and rang a total of 23 peals on the bells at Brant Broughton!

All the members of this band either rung with Phil or knew him well. He was a true gent and he will be greatly missed by all who knew him. Our thoughts are with his wife Kath and the rest of his family at this difficult time.

This quarter was intended to be rung at Brant Broughton, however on arrival at Brant Broughton this evening it was discovered that the fourth was unringable due to a badly damaged wheel. We are therefore very grateful to Fran Brealey, Churchwarden at Welbourn for allowing us with no notice at all (10 mins notice) to come and ring the quarter on the back six at neighboring Welbourn instead!

Rung prior to the North Kesteven District Council Chairman’s Civic Service.

In attendance was Her Majesty’s Lord-Lieutenant for the County of Lincolnshire, Mr Tony Worth; Chairman of North Kesteven District Council, Councillor Raymond Cucksey; High Sheriff of Lincolnshire, Mr John Burke Esq; the Right Worshipful the Mayor of Lincoln, Councillor Karen Lee; the City Sheriff, Mrs Melanie Tointon; Commandant of RAF College Cranwell, Air Commodore David Stubbs; Station Commander of RAF Waddington, Group Captain Al Gillespie; Station Commander of RAF Coningsby, Group Captain Martin Sampson; Chief Constable of Lincolnshire Police, Mr Neil Rhodes; Chief Fire Office of Lincolnshire Fire & Rescue, Mr Dave Ramscar; Rural Dean of Lafford & Chaplain to North Kesteven District Council, Reverend Christine Pennock; along with Members of Parliament for Lincolnshire; Mayor’s from around the County; Councillors from Lincolnshire & Nottinghamshire County Councils; members of the City of Lincoln Civic Party and other County and visiting Dignitaries.

The bells were also rung for 15 minutes immediately after the service, consisting of rounds and call changes – ‘sixty on thirds’, whilst the Civic Procession, visiting Dignitaries and congregation left the Church to attend Afternoon Tea at nearby Branston Hall Hotel.

On July 4th 1862 two Oxford fellows, Charles Lutwidge Dodgson of Christ Church and Robinson Duckworth of Trinity, took a rowing boat on the Isis from Folly Bridge, near Christ Church, to Godstow with the three daughters of Henry Liddell, the Dean of Christ Church and later Vice Chancellor of the University. During their voyage, Dodgson entertained the girls with a story he made up featuring the second daughter, Alice, and her search for adventure. The girls loved the story so much that they urged him to write it down. Under the pseudonym Lewis Carroll he did so, and called it "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland".

Specially arranged and rung half muffled by a local band in affectionate memory of Gwendoline Maud Walker “Gwen” who sadly passed away on 19th July 2012 at the age of 94. Today would have been Gwen’s 95th birthday.
Gwen has been Verge here at St. Andrew’s for many years as well as sitting on the PCC. She was a great supporter of the Church and a loyal member of the congregation.

Gwen was also a great supporter of the bells, especially during the time after the Millennium when we were fundraising to rehang our three bells and augment them to six and she loved to hear the bells being rung. She was a good friend to the ringers and always came into the belfry on a Sunday morning to say hello and wish us well. She will be greatly missed by us all.

Rung also remembering Leslie Walker, Gwen’s late husband, who was also a great supporter of the Church and a loyal member of the congregation, who passed away three years ago, both of whom are now reunited.

Rung to mark the 50th anniversary of the bells being rung for the first time less than a week after the devastating fire on Christmas Day 1962. The Church was unusable after the fire but thankfully the tower and bells suffered little damage with just the bell ropes being burnt through. The local ringers borrowed and spliced old ropes so that the bells could be rung the following Sunday after Christmas (the Sunday after the fire), with the service being held in the neighbouring Methodist Chapel.

Local ringer Ron Applewhite age 92 was a member of the local band when the fire happened being the Tower Secretary, and is now the only surviving member of the original Branston band. We were delighted to see Ron ringing with us before this morning’s service.

Specially arranged & rung by family & friends to congratulate our Tower Captain, J Geoffrey Burton, on being awarded an MBE (for services to bell ringing in North Staffordshire) in the New Year's Honours List.

Geoff has been Tower Captain here for 55½yrs. He has served terms as Secretary, Chairman & Bell Adviser for the N Staffs Association. He is the Diocesan Bell Adviser for the DAC at Lichfield, attending meetings when anything connected with church bells comes up on the Agenda. He has attended several National Conferences for Bell Advisers.

Geoff has a great knowledge & a vast experience of bells, bell founders, bell frames & bell installations. He has carried very many inspections of bell towers in the Lichfield Diocese & has reported wisely to PCC meetings in many parishes. He was responsible for getting the lumpy old ring of 8 here at St Peter's, recast in 1971 by Taylors into a new ring of 10 bells, hung lower in the tower He is well known & respected amonsgst bell ringers everywhere. Well done, Geoffrey; Congratulations!!!

This peal was rung whilst the celebratory lunch in the Village Hall was taking place after this morning’s special service attended by the Lord Bishop of Lincoln, the Right Reverend Christopher Lowson and George Miles Hobart-Hampden, 10th Earl of Buckinghamshire, representing the Hobart family and who is a descendant of the Countess of Ripon.

Rung by the Sunday Service band prior to the special service to celebrate the 150th anniversary of the Consecration of All Saints Church Nocton on 16th December 1862 by the Right Reverend John Jackson, 59th Lord Bishop of Lincoln. Today’s service was attended by the present Lord Bishop of Lincoln, the Right Reverend Christopher Lowson and George Miles Hobart-Hampden, 10th Earl of Buckinghamshire, representing the Hobart family and who is a descendant of the Countess of Ripon.

The Church was rebuilt through the generosity of Lady Sarah Albinia Louisa Robinson (Nee Hobart), Countess of Ripon, daughter of the 4th Earl of Buckinghamshire, as a memorial to her late husband, Lord Frederick John Robinson, first Earl of Ripon, who owned Nocton Estate & Hall.
The bells were also rung for 20 minutes immediately after the service as the congregation made its way from the Church to the celebratory lunch in the Village Hall.
